chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But upon those who take him as a guardian.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardians/protectors

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority is not absolute over all believers but is conditional upon their voluntary submission, specifically those who take him as a guardian (wali). This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of *taklif* (accountability), where spiritual dominion is earned through adherence rather than imposed by nature. The narration reinforces the concept of *wilayah* by contrasting divine guardianship with satanic influence, highlighting the believer's agency in choosing their spiritual master.
